compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The mcp blue-green deploy block documents itself as INDEPENDENT of the review-bot block above
it, but it sits AFTER that block's `exit 0`. When the review-bot is busy, the deferral path
terminates the whole script, so the mcp deploy never runs. The documented independence is false
in the only case where it matters — a shared `src/rebar` change, which triggers BOTH triggers.

## The coupling, in the code

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`:

- `:140` `BOT_PATHS` and `:152` `MCP_PATHS` both begin with `src/rebar`, so any library change
  matches BOTH.
- `:506` `if changed "$BOT_PATHS" || changed "$SECRETS_PATHS"; then` — enters the bot block.
- `:530-541` when `in_flight > 0` and the episode is under `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX`, it emits
  `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED` and **`exit 0`** — terminating the PROCESS, not just the bot block.
- `:616-621` the mcp block's own header states:

      # INDEPENDENT of the review-bot block above: a shared src/rebar / docker-compose.yml
      # change triggers both, each on its own path. Unlike the review-bot's stop-and-drain,
      # the mcp server is a never-idle shared endpoint ... and NEVER kills an in-flight
      # certified op.

  It is unreachable whenever the bot block deferred. The blue-green design exists precisely so
  the mcp endpoint never waits on an in-flight review (`:120`), and that property is defeated by
  control flow one screen above it.

## Observed impact (2026-08-26)

Two commits merged at 06:47Z — `84fc5f9b68df` (library reads error on an absent store) and
`30d7059f632d` (the mcp secrets-refresh fix). Forty minutes later neither was running: a live
probe of the deployed MCP server still returned the OLD behaviour (`list_tickets` -> `[]`
instead of erroring).

`rebar/host` metrics, 60s period, show every tick deferring:

    deploy_deferrals  07:12Z=3.0  07:18Z=3.0  07:24Z=2.0
    deploy_errors     07:12Z=2.0  07:18Z=0    07:24Z=0

The observability probe runs every 5 min and autodeploy every 2 min, so 2-3 deferrals per probe
interval is ~100% of ticks.

The deferral marker is itself the proof the script got past the up-to-date check (`:470-476`)
and matched a real delta — so this is not a stale `deployed-sha`, not a mirror-fetch failure,
and not the SHA-keyed backoff (`:479-483`, which exits at `:481` BEFORE the deferral marker).

**Why the bot is chronically busy:** all six open Gerrit changes sit at `LLM-Review = 0`. The
review bot drains a queue with a SINGLE worker (`review_bot/app.py:80`), so ordinary pipelining
keeps `in_flight > 0` essentially always. `autodeploy.sh:89-97` (bug 7b4a) already documents
that the bound "is reasoned about as if it were a single-review timer" and "was outlasted by
ordinary PIPELINING" — this ticket is that same saturation now blocking a path that was
explicitly designed not to wait.

**The circularity worth naming:** `30d7059f632d` is itself the mcp deploy fix, and it cannot
deploy because of this. Change 2232 — which adds the `/health` store signal that would make a
storeless deploy diagnosable — is queued in the same saturated review queue.

## Why the alarm did not catch it

`rebar-autodeploy-errors` is Sum over 900s with 3-of-4 datapoints and `notBreaching` on missing
data, so an isolated failure cannot alarm by construction. It read OK throughout. A green alarm
is not evidence of a healthy deploy here.

## Proposed fix

Scope the deferral to the bot block instead of terminating the script: set a flag (e.g.
`bot_deferred=1`) and `continue` past the remainder of the bot block, letting control reach the
mcp block. The mcp path is a pointer-swap that never kills an in-flight op, so there is no
reason for it to wait on the bot's drain.

Take care that the deferral episode bookkeeping (`DEFER_FILE`, `:538`) and the
`record_backoff_failure` semantics stay unchanged for the bot path, and that a bot deferral
still results in the same exit status the timer expects when the mcp block also does nothing.

## Test gap that let this through

`tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:144` stubs `git diff` to report ONLY
`infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` as changed, so `changed "$BOT_PATHS"` is always false and the mcp
block always runs in isolation. The real case — a shared `src/rebar` change triggering both
blocks while the bot is busy — is never exercised. The sibling suite
`tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py` has coverage of the drain gate but none
asserting the mcp target stays reachable across a deferral.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A tick where the review-bot block DEFERS still reaches the mcp blue-green block, so a
      shared `src/rebar` change deploys the mcp service without waiting on the bot's drain.
- [ ] The bot path's deferral bookkeeping (episode file, bound, markers) and backoff semantics
      are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression coverage drives a tick with BOTH triggers matching and the bot busy, asserting
      the mcp container is still deployed — the case the current stub makes unreachable.
- [ ] The stub in `test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` no longer forces bot-block-false, or a new
      test supplies a git stub reporting a shared `src/rebar` change.

## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q -p no:randomly
    bash -n infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh && shellcheck -S error infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh

The new coverage has teeth when: with the `exit 0` restored in the deferral path, the new
both-triggers test FAILS (no mcp deploy), and with the scoped-`continue` fix it PASSES.

file_impact.reason: Scope the review-bot deferral to that block (flag + skip the rest of the bot block) instead of exit 0, so control reaches the mcp blue-green block which is documented as independent and never waits on an in-flight review

Drive a tick with BOTH triggers matching and the bot busy: the mcp deploy must still happen. The current git stub reports only Dockerfile.mcp so the bot block is never entered, which is why this regressed unnoticed

compiled_state.title: autodeploy: a review-bot deferral exit 0s the script, so the 'independent' mcp blue-green deploy never runs
